patch_description: Extends the current multi-pass Steiner-like approach with a throughput feasibility check on heavily-shared trunk edges. In `route_pass`, we track how many destinations route over each edge; once aggregate demand (dest_count × per-dst flow) exceeds the edge's throughput, we restore the original cost for subsequent Dijkstra runs so later destinations route around the saturated edge. This prevents silent capacity violations that gate cost_score. Per prior evidence, throughput is used only as a hard feasibility filter, never as load-spreading (which cost 5–10%). We keep the candidate-ordering search and refinement passes, but pass per-dst flow (estimated as num_partitions) into the feasibility check.
